founderDecisionRecommendations.1-angelos-angel: Endorse. ἄγγελος is the technical term for a heavenly envoy in first-century Jewish Greek (BDAG s.v. 2); published Mt 1, 13, 25, 28, Acts 12 and the Revelation wave all print 'angel', so the Greek NT is already harmonized in practice. Promote jointly with Revelation as a central Greek-NT convention; keep 'messenger of YHWH' for Hebrew malʾāḵ.
founderDecisionRecommendations.2-naos-sanctuary: Endorse for Matthew. The naos/hieron distinction is lexical (BDAG; Josephus) and NRSV marks it in 23:16-35. 27:5 keeps Matthew's crux honestly (and, to my reading, restores the ASV's own 'sanctuary'). If promoted, scope it to books with both terms; Revelation's 'temple' for ναός is defensible because it has no ἱερόν.
founderDecisionRecommendations.3-23:14-no-paragraph: Endorse. SBLGNT has no 23:14; the Byzantine text is quoted in full at 23:13 with witnesses, as the 6:13b precedent and the Revelation ruling C require. Recommend a later pass bring the stable 17:21 into line: its bracketed Greek is not SBLGNT text, so drop the paragraph and move the Byzantine wording into the 17:20 commentary.

founderDecisionRecommendations.6-faithfulness-23:23: Endorse. BDAG lists Mt 23:23 under πίστις 1a 'faithfulness, reliability'; NIV and ESV render so; the Mic 6:8 triad is conduct.
founderDecisionRecommendations.7-put-at-my-disposal-26:53: Endorse. BDAG παρίστημι 1a cites this verse for 'put at someone's disposal', and the NASB prints exactly 'put at My disposal'; the ground is independent of the canon's French, and the coincidence is disclosed.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάντας τοὺς λόγους τούτους, εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ·

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples:

notes.official: 'when Jesus had finished all these words': the closing formula of the fifth and last discourse (cf. 7:28; 11:1; 13:53; 19:1), here with 'all', which some commentators read as an echo of Deut 31:1; 32:45.

paragraphs.text: Οἴδατε ὅτι μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας τὸ πάσχα γίνεται, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς τὸ σταυρωθῆναι.
paragraphs.translit: oidate hoti meta dyo hēmeras to pascha ginetai, kai ho huios tou anthrōpou paradidotai eis to staurōthēnai.

i18n.en: "You know that after two days the Passover is coming, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified."

notes.official: *paradidotai* 'is handed over': a present tense for the certain future (`son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: Τότε συνήχθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως τοῦ λεγομένου Καϊάφα,
paragraphs.translit: tote synēchthēsan hoi archiereis kai hoi presbyteroi tou laou eis tēn aulēn tou archiereōs tou legomenou kaiapha,

i18n.en: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people were gathered together in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,

notes.official: 'the chief priests and the elders of the people' (critical text). The Byzantine text and the KJV add *kai hoi grammateis* 'and the scribes'. Similar Byzantine expansions add 'and the elders' at 26:59 and 'false witnesses' at 26:60 (`critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`). *eis tēn aulēn* 'in the courtyard' (ASV 'court'); *Kaiapha*, high priest 18-36 CE (Josephus, Ant. 18.35, 95).

paragraphs.translit: elegon de· mē en tē heortē, hina mē thorybos genētai en tō laō.

i18n.en: But they were saying: "Not during the feast, lest there be an uproar among the people."

paragraphs.text: Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ γενομένου ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ,
paragraphs.translit: tou de iēsou genomenou en bēthania en oikia simōnos tou leprou,

i18n.en: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,

paragraphs.text: προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ γυνὴ ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου βαρυτίμου καὶ κατέχεεν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου.
paragraphs.translit: prosēlthen autō gynē echousa alabastron myrou barytimou kai katecheen epi tēs kephalēs autou anakeimenou.

i18n.en: a woman came to him having an alabaster jar of very costly ointment, and she poured it on his head as he reclined at table.

notes.official: *alabastron* 'an alabaster jar': a flask of fine stone for perfume, broken at the neck to pour.

paragraphs.text: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἠγανάκτησαν λέγοντες· Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη;
paragraphs.translit: idontes de hoi mathētai ēganaktēsan legontes· eis ti hē apōleia hautē;

i18n.en: But when the disciples saw it, they were indignant, saying: "To what purpose is this waste?

paragraphs.text: ἐδύνατο γὰρ τοῦτο πραθῆναι πολλοῦ καὶ δοθῆναι πτωχοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: edynato gar touto prathēnai pollou kai dothēnai ptōchois.

i18n.en: For this could have been sold for much and given to the poor."

paragraphs.text: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί κόπους παρέχετε τῇ γυναικί; ἔργον γὰρ καλὸν ἠργάσατο εἰς ἐμέ·
paragraphs.translit: gnous de ho iēsous eipen autois· ti kopous parechete tē gynaiki; ergon gar kalon ērgasato eis eme·

i18n.en: But Jesus, knowing it, said to them: "Why do you trouble the woman? For she has done a beautiful work for me.

paragraphs.text: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε·
paragraphs.translit: pantote gar tous ptōchous echete methʼ heautōn, eme de ou pantote echete·

i18n.en: For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.

notes.official: 'you always have the poor with you': cf. Deut 15:11.

paragraphs.text: βαλοῦσα γὰρ αὕτη τὸ μύρον τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ σώματός μου πρὸς τὸ ἐνταφιάσαι με ἐποίησεν.
paragraphs.translit: balousa gar hautē to myron touto epi tou sōmatos mou pros to entaphiasai me epoiēsen.

i18n.en: For in pouring this ointment on my body, she has done it to prepare me for burial.

paragraphs.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦτο ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ, λαληθήσεται καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin, hopou ean kērychthē to euangelion touto en holō tō kosmō, lalēthēsetai kai ho epoiēsen hautē eis mnēmosynon autēs.

i18n.en: Amen I say to you, wherever this gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be told in memory of her."

notes.official: *hopou ean kērychthē to euangelion touto* 'wherever this gospel is proclaimed' (`euangelion-gospel-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: Τότε πορευθεὶς εἷς τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριώτης, πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς
paragraphs.translit: tote poreutheis heis tōn dōdeka, ho legomenos ioudas iskariōtēs, pros tous archiereis

i18n.en: Then one of the twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests

paragraphs.text: εἶπεν· Τί θέλετέ μοι δοῦναι κἀγὼ ὑμῖν παραδώσω αὐτόν; οἱ δὲ ἔστησαν αὐτῷ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια.
paragraphs.translit: eipen· ti thelete moi dounai kagō hymin paradōsō auton; hoi de estēsan autō triakonta argyria.

i18n.en: and said: "What are you willing to give me, and I will hand him over to you?" And they weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver.

notes.official: *estēsan autō triakonta argyria* 'they weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver': Zech 11:12, quoted explicitly at 27:9-10. *histēmi* 'weigh' is the LXX sense in Zechariah.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀπὸ τότε ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai apo tote ezētei eukairian hina auton paradō.

i18n.en: And from that time he was seeking an opportunity to hand him over.

paragraphs.text: Τῇ δὲ πρώτῃ τῶν ἀζύμων προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες· Ποῦ θέλεις ἑτοιμάσωμέν σοι φαγεῖν τὸ πάσχα;
paragraphs.translit: tē de prōtē tōn azymōn prosēlthon hoi mathētai tō iēsou legontes· pou theleis hetoimasōmen soi phagein to pascha;

i18n.en: Now on the first day of Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying: "Where do you wish us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?"

notes.official: *tē de prōtē tōn azymōn* 'on the first day of Unleavened Bread'.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν πόλιν πρὸς τὸν δεῖνα καὶ εἴπατε αὐτῷ· Ὁ διδάσκαλος λέγει· Ὁ καιρός μου ἐγγύς ἐστιν· πρὸς σὲ ποιῶ τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· hypagete eis tēn polin pros ton deina kai eipate autō· ho didaskalos legei· ho kairos mou engys estin· pros se poiō to pascha meta tōn mathētōn mou.

i18n.en: And he said: "Go into the city to such a one, and say to him: 'The Teacher says: "My time is near; I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples."'"

notes.official: *Ho kairos mou engys estin* 'My time is near'. The colons at both levels follow this wave's convention (`speech-introduction-colon-convention-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐποίησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὡς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.
paragraphs.translit: kai epoiēsan hoi mathētai hōs synetaxen autois ho iēsous, kai hētoimasan to pascha.

i18n.en: And the disciples did as Jesus had directed them, and they prepared the Passover.

paragraphs.text: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης ἀνέκειτο μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα μαθητῶν
paragraphs.translit: opsias de genomenēs anekeito meta tōn dōdeka mathētōn

i18n.en: Now when evening had come, he was reclining at table with the twelve disciples.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐσθιόντων αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν παραδώσει με.
paragraphs.translit: kai esthiontōn autōn eipen· amēn legō hymin hoti heis ex hymōn paradōsei me.

i18n.en: And as they were eating, he said: "Amen I say to you that one of you will hand me over."

paragraphs.text: καὶ λυπούμενοι σφόδρα ἤρξαντο λέγειν αὐτῷ εἷς ἕκαστος· Μήτι ἐγώ εἰμι, κύριε;
paragraphs.translit: kai lypoumenoi sphodra ērxanto legein autō heis hekastos· mēti egō eimi, kyrie;

i18n.en: And being exceedingly sorrowful, they began to say to him, each one: "Surely it is not I, Lord?"

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ὁ ἐμβάψας μετʼ ἐμοῦ τὴν χεῖρα ἐν τῷ τρυβλίῳ οὗτός με παραδώσει·
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· ho embapsas metʼ emou tēn cheira en tō trybliō houtos me paradōsei·

i18n.en: And he answered and said: "The one who has dipped his hand in the dish with me, this one will hand me over.

paragraphs.text: ὁ μὲν υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑπάγει καθὼς γέγραπται περὶ αὐτοῦ, οὐαὶ δὲ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ διʼ οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται· καλὸν ἦν αὐτῷ εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος.
paragraphs.translit: ho men huios tou anthrōpou hypagei kathōs gegraptai peri autou, ouai de tō anthrōpō ekeinō diʼ hou ho huios tou anthrōpou paradidotai· kalon ēn autō ei ouk egennēthē ho anthrōpos ekeinos.

i18n.en: The Son of Man goes as it is written of him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been good for that man if he had not been born."

paragraphs.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν εἶπεν· Μήτι ἐγώ εἰμι, ῥαββί; λέγει αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶπας.
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ioudas ho paradidous auton eipen· mēti egō eimi, rhabbi; legei autō· sy eipas.

i18n.en: And Judas, who was handing him over, answered and said: "Surely it is not I, Rabbi?" He says to him: "You have said it."

notes.official: *Sy eipas* 'You have said it': an affirmative answer that leaves the responsibility with the questioner; the same reply to the high priest at 26:64 (cf. 27:11 *Sy legeis*).

paragraphs.text: Ἐσθιόντων δὲ αὐτῶν λαβὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἄρτον καὶ εὐλογήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ δοὺς τοῖς μαθηταῖς εἶπεν· Λάβετε φάγετε, τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου.
paragraphs.translit: esthiontōn de autōn labōn ho iēsous arton kai eulogēsas eklasen kai dous tois mathētais eipen· labete phagete, touto estin to sōma mou.

i18n.en: And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and having blessed it he broke it, and giving it to the disciples he said: "Take, eat; this is my body."

notes.official: *eulogēsas* 'having blessed it' (cf. 14:19); *eucharistēsas* 'having given thanks' in 26:27.

paragraphs.text: καὶ λαβὼν ποτήριον καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Πίετε ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες,
paragraphs.translit: kai labōn potērion kai eucharistēsas edōken autois legōn· piete ex autou pantes,

i18n.en: And he took a cup, and having given thanks he gave it to them, saying: "Drink from it, all of you;

paragraphs.text: τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά μου τῆς διαθήκης τὸ περὶ πολλῶν ἐκχυννόμενον εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν·
paragraphs.translit: touto gar estin to haima mou tēs diathēkēs to peri pollōn ekchynnomenon eis aphesin hamartiōn·

i18n.en: for this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

notes.official: *to haima mou tēs diathēkēs* 'my blood of the covenant': the phrase of Exod 24:8 LXX, the blood that seals the covenant at Sinai. *diathēkē* renders Hebrew *bərît* in the LXX and is rendered 'covenant', in agreement with the Hebrew-side central entries (`brit-covenant`, `karat-brit-cut-covenant`). The Byzantine text and the KJV add *kainēs* 'new' (KJV 'the new testament'), from Luke 22:20 and 1 Cor 11:25, and 'testament' comes from Latin *testamentum* (`diatheke-covenant-mt-26-28`; `critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`). *eis aphesin hamartiōn* 'for the forgiveness of sins' is Matthew's own addition to Mark 14:24.

paragraphs.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ πίω ἀπʼ ἄρτι ἐκ τούτου τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ὅταν αὐτὸ πίνω μεθʼ ὑμῶν καινὸν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρός μου.
paragraphs.translit: legō de hymin, ou mē piō apʼ arti ek toutou tou genēmatos tēs ampelou heōs tēs hēmeras ekeinēs hotan auto pinō methʼ hymōn kainon en tē basileia tou patros mou.

i18n.en: And I say to you, I will not drink from now on of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father."

notes.official: *ek toutou tou genēmatos tēs ampelou* 'of this fruit of the vine': the blessing formula over wine ('who creates the fruit of the vine').

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὑμνήσαντες ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hymnēsantes exēlthon eis to oros tōn elaiōn.

i18n.en: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

notes.official: *hymnēsantes* 'when they had sung a hymn': probably the second part of the Hallel (Ps 113-118), sung at the end of the Passover meal.

paragraphs.text: Τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πάντες ὑμεῖς σκανδαλισθήσεσθε ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ταύτῃ, γέγραπται γάρ· Πατάξω τὸν ποιμένα, καὶ διασκορπισθήσονται τὰ πρόβατα τῆς ποίμνης·
paragraphs.translit: tote legei autois ho iēsous· pantes hymeis skandalisthēsesthe en emoi en tē nykti tautē, gegraptai gar· pataxō ton poimena, kai diaskorpisthēsontai ta probata tēs poimnēs·

i18n.en: Then Jesus says to them: "All of you will fall away because of me this night; for it is written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.'

notes.official: *Pantes hymeis skandalisthēsesthe en emoi* 'All of you will fall away because of me': the passive of *skandalizō* in the sense of abandoning allegiance, as at the published 13:21; it is fulfilled at 26:56 ('all the disciples left him and fled'). The ASV and KJV have 'be offended in me' (`skandalizo-fall-away-take-offense-matthew`). Zech 13:7: the MT has an imperative ('Strike the shepherd'), Matthew a first-person future ('I will strike'), making God the agent. The colon follows this wave's convention (`speech-introduction-colon-convention-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: μετὰ δὲ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με προάξω ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
paragraphs.translit: meta de to egerthēnai me proaxō hymas eis tēn galilaian.

i18n.en: But after I have been raised, I will go before you into Galilee."

paragraphs.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ πάντες σκανδαλισθήσονται ἐν σοί, ἐγὼ οὐδέποτε σκανδαλισθήσομαι.
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho petros eipen autō· ei pantes skandalisthēsontai en soi, egō oudepote skandalisthēsomai.

i18n.en: But Peter answered and said to him: "Though all fall away because of you, I will never fall away."

notes.official: 'fall away' twice, as in 26:31 (`skandalizo-fall-away-take-offense-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρὶς ἀπαρνήσῃ με.
paragraphs.translit: ephē autō ho iēsous· amēn legō soi hoti en tautē tē nykti prin alektora phōnēsai tris aparnēsē me.

i18n.en: Jesus said to him: "Amen I say to you that this very night, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times."

paragraphs.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος· Κἂν δέῃ με σὺν σοὶ ἀποθανεῖν, οὐ μή σε ἀπαρνήσομαι. ὁμοίως καὶ πάντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō ho petros· kan deē me syn soi apothanein, ou mē se aparnēsomai. homoiōs kai pantes hoi mathētai eipan.

i18n.en: Peter says to him: "Even if I must die with you, I will by no means deny you." And all the disciples said the same.

paragraphs.text: Τότε ἔρχεται μετʼ αὐτῶν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς χωρίον λεγόμενον Γεθσημανί, καὶ λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς· Καθίσατε αὐτοῦ ἕως οὗ ἀπελθὼν ἐκεῖ προσεύξωμαι.
paragraphs.translit: tote erchetai metʼ autōn ho iēsous eis chōrion legomenon gethsēmani, kai legei tois mathētais· kathisate autou heōs hou apelthōn ekei proseuxōmai.

i18n.en: Then Jesus comes with them to a place called Gethsemane, and he says to the disciples: "Sit here while I go over there and pray."

paragraphs.text: καὶ παραλαβὼν τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς δύο υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου ἤρξατο λυπεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai paralabōn ton petron kai tous dyo huious zebedaiou ērxato lypeisthai kai adēmonein.

i18n.en: And taking with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed.

paragraphs.text: τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς· Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου· μείνατε ὧδε καὶ γρηγορεῖτε μετʼ ἐμοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: tote legei autois· perilypos estin hē psychē mou heōs thanatou· meinate hōde kai grēgoreite metʼ emou.

i18n.en: Then he says to them: "My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death; remain here and keep watch with me."

notes.official: *Perilypos estin hē psychē mou heōs thanatou* 'My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death': the words of Ps 42:6, 12; 43:5 (41:6, 12; 42:5 LXX). *psychē* as the seat of emotion is rendered 'soul' (`psyche-soul-life-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: καὶ προελθὼν μικρὸν ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ προσευχόμενος καὶ λέγων· Πάτερ μου, εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν, παρελθάτω ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο· πλὴν οὐχ ὡς ἐγὼ θέλω ἀλλʼ ὡς σύ.
paragraphs.translit: kai proelthōn mikron epesen epi prosōpon autou proseuchomenos kai legōn· pater mou, ei dynaton estin, parelthatō apʼ emou to potērion touto· plēn ouch hōs egō thelō allʼ hōs sy.

i18n.en: And going a little farther, he fell on his face, praying and saying: "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me; yet not as I will, but as you will."

notes.official: *to potērion touto* 'this cup': the cup of suffering and of God's wrath (Isa 51:17; Jer 25:15). *plēn ouch hōs egō thelō all' hōs sy* 'yet not as I will, but as you will'.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ εὑρίσκει αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, καὶ λέγει τῷ Πέτρῳ· Οὕτως οὐκ ἰσχύσατε μίαν ὥραν γρηγορῆσαι μετʼ ἐμοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: kai erchetai pros tous mathētas kai heuriskei autous katheudontas, kai legei tō petrō· houtōs ouk ischysate mian hōran grēgorēsai metʼ emou;

i18n.en: And he comes to the disciples and finds them sleeping, and he says to Peter: "So, were you not able to keep watch with me one hour?

paragraphs.text: γρηγορεῖτε καὶ προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν· τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής.
paragraphs.translit: grēgoreite kai proseuchesthe, hina mē eiselthēte eis peirasmon· to men pneuma prothymon hē de sarx asthenēs.

i18n.en: Keep watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation; the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak."

notes.official: *hina mē eiselthēte eis peirasmon* 'that you may not enter into temptation': *peirasmos* is rendered 'temptation', as in the published 6:13 (`peirazo-peirasmos-tempt-test-matthew`). *to men pneuma prothymon hē de sarx asthenēs* 'the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak': the human spirit, lower case (`pneuma-spirit-capitalization-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο λέγων· Πάτερ μου, εἰ οὐ δύναται τοῦτο παρελθεῖν ἐὰν μὴ αὐτὸ πίω, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου.
paragraphs.translit: palin ek deuterou apelthōn prosēuxato legōn· pater mou, ei ou dynatai touto parelthein ean mē auto piō, genēthētō to thelēma sou.

i18n.en: Again, a second time, he went away and prayed, saying: "My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, let your will be done."

notes.official: *ei ou dynatai touto parelthein ean mē auto piō* 'if this cannot pass unless I drink it' (critical text). The Byzantine text and the KJV add *to potērion* and *ap' emou* ('if this cup may not pass away from me'), clarifying from 26:39 (`critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`). *genēthētō to thelēma sou* 'let your will be done' is word for word the third petition of the Lord's Prayer (the published 6:10).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν πάλιν εὗρεν αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, ἦσαν γὰρ αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ βεβαρημένοι.
paragraphs.translit: kai elthōn palin heuren autous katheudontas, ēsan gar autōn hoi ophthalmoi bebarēmenoi.

i18n.en: And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς πάλιν ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο ἐκ τρίτου τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπὼν πάλιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apheis autous palin apelthōn prosēuxato ek tritou ton auton logon eipōn palin.

i18n.en: And leaving them, he went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same word again.

paragraphs.text: τότε ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Καθεύδετε τὸ λοιπὸν καὶ ἀναπαύεσθε· ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ἡ ὥρα καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἁμαρτωλῶν.
paragraphs.translit: tote erchetai pros tous mathētas kai legei autois· katheudete to loipon kai anapauesthe· idou ēngiken hē hōra kai ho huios tou anthrōpou paradidotai eis cheiras hamartōlōn.

i18n.en: Then he comes to the disciples and says to them: "Sleep on now and take your rest. Behold, the hour has come near, and the Son of Man is handed over into the hands of sinners.

notes.official: *Katheudete loipon kai anapauesthe* 'Sleep on now and take your rest': the Greek can also be read as a question ('Are you still sleeping and taking your rest?'), as in the RSV and NRSV. The ASV and KJV imperative is kept (`son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: ἐγείρεσθε ἄγωμεν· ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ὁ παραδιδούς με.
paragraphs.translit: egeiresthe agōmen· idou ēngiken ho paradidous me.

i18n.en: Rise, let us be going; behold, the one who hands me over has come near."

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ἦλθεν καὶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ὄχλος πολὺς μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων ἀπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τοῦ λαοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eti autou lalountos idou ioudas heis tōn dōdeka ēlthen kai metʼ autou ochlos polys meta machairōn kai xylōn apo tōn archiereōn kai presbyterōn tou laou.

i18n.en: And while he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς σημεῖον λέγων· Ὃν ἂν φιλήσω αὐτός ἐστιν· κρατήσατε αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de paradidous auton edōken autois sēmeion legōn· hon an philēsō autos estin· kratēsate auton.

i18n.en: Now the one who was handing him over had given them a sign, saying: "Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him."

paragraphs.text: καὶ εὐθέως προσελθὼν τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἶπεν· Χαῖρε, ῥαββί· καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eutheōs proselthōn tō iēsou eipen· chaire, rhabbi· kai katephilēsen auton.

i18n.en: And immediately he came up to Jesus and said: "Greetings, Rabbi!" And he kissed him.

notes.official: *Chaire, rhabbi* 'Greetings, Rabbi!': *chaire* is the ordinary greeting, the same word as the risen Jesus' greeting to the women at the published 28:9.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἑταῖρε, ἐφʼ ὃ πάρει. τότε προσελθόντες ἐπέβαλον τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐκράτησαν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de iēsous eipen autō· hetaire, ephʼ ho parei. tote proselthontes epebalon tas cheiras epi ton iēsoun kai ekratēsan auton.

i18n.en: But Jesus said to him: "Friend, do that for which you have come." Then they came and laid hands on Jesus and seized him.

notes.official: *Hetaire, eph' ho parei* 'Friend, do that for which you have come': the phrase is elliptical. It can be a command with an imperative supplied (ASV, NRSV), a question (KJV 'wherefore art thou come?'; RSV 'why are you here?'), though the interrogative use of *hos* is rare, or an exclamation ('so that is what you are here for!'). Drinking cups inscribed *euphrainou eph' ho parei* ('enjoy yourself; that is what you are here for') suggest a fixed idiom (Deissmann, Light from the Ancient East). The command fits Matthew's portrait of Jesus in control of the passion and is kept (`hetaire-eph-ho-parei-mt-26-50`; Brown, The Death of the Messiah, ad loc.). *hetairos* 'friend, comrade' is used only by Matthew, always to someone in the wrong (20:13; 22:12).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ εἷς τῶν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπέσπασεν τὴν μάχαιραν αὐτοῦ καὶ πατάξας τὸν δοῦλον τοῦ ἀρχιερέως ἀφεῖλεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτίον.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou heis tōn meta iēsou ekteinas tēn cheira apespasen tēn machairan autou kai pataxas ton doulon tou archiereōs apheilen autou to ōtion.

i18n.en: And behold, one of those who were with Jesus stretched out his hand and drew his sword, and striking the slave of the high priest, he cut off his ear.

notes.official: *ton doulon tou archiereōs* 'the slave of the high priest'; John 18:10 names him Malchus and the swordsman Peter.

paragraphs.text: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀπόστρεψον τὴν μάχαιράν σου εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς, πάντες γὰρ οἱ λαβόντες μάχαιραν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀπολοῦνται·
paragraphs.translit: tote legei autō ho iēsous· apostrepson tēn machairan sou eis ton topon autēs, pantes gar hoi labontes machairan en machairē apolountai·

i18n.en: Then Jesus says to him: "Put your sword back into its place; for all who take the sword will perish by the sword.

notes.official: *Apostrepson tēn machairan sou eis ton topon autēs* 'Put your sword back into its place'. See the reception note at 26:53, which covers 26:52-54.

paragraphs.text: ἢ δοκεῖς ὅτι οὐ δύναμαι παρακαλέσαι τὸν πατέρα μου, καὶ παραστήσει μοι ἄρτι πλείω δώδεκα λεγιῶνας ἀγγέλων;
paragraphs.translit: ē dokeis hoti ou dynamai parakalesai ton patera mou, kai parastēsei moi arti pleiō dōdeka legiōnas angelōn;

i18n.en: Or do you think that I cannot appeal to my Father, and he will at once put at my disposal more than twelve legions of angels?

notes.official:
*parakalesai ton patera mou* 'appeal to my Father' (BDAG s.v. *parakaleō* 3; ASV 'beseech'). *parastēsei moi* 'he will put at my disposal': *paristēmi* means 'place beside, put at someone's disposal', and BDAG cites this verse for that sense (s.v. 1a). The draft and the ASV had 'send me', a paraphrase of the result; Greek uses other verbs for 'send' (*apostellō*, 13:41; 24:31) (`paristemi-put-at-disposal-mt-26-53`). *legiōnas* 'legions': a Latin loanword, a Roman legion numbering about 6,000 men. *angelōn* 'angels' (`angelos-angel-matthew-convention`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 4) quotes 26:52-54 (« Remets ton sabre en place (…). Crois-tu que je ne pourrais pas faire appel à mon père, qui mettrait à l'instant à ma disposition plus de douze légions d'anges ? Mais comment seraient remplies les écritures ? Car il doit en être ainsi ») and reads it as Jesus revealing the importance of his death and of the scriptures that would later bear witness, so that the creators, when they return, will be recognized and not taken for invaders. The canon's « faire appel » and « mettre à ma disposition » agree with the lexical senses adopted here; the change rests on BDAG, and the agreement is recorded.

paragraphs.text: πῶς οὖν πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ ὅτι οὕτως δεῖ γενέσθαι;
paragraphs.translit: pōs oun plērōthōsin hai graphai hoti houtōs dei genesthai;

i18n.en: How then would the scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen in this way?"

notes.official: *hoti houtōs dei genesthai* 'that it must happen in this way': *dei* expresses divine necessity, as in the passion predictions (16:21). See the reception note at 26:53.

paragraphs.text: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων συλλαβεῖν με; καθʼ ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐκαθεζόμην διδάσκων καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με.
paragraphs.translit: en ekeinē tē hōra eipen ho iēsous tois ochlois· hōs epi lēstēn exēlthate meta machairōn kai xylōn syllabein me; kathʼ hēmeran en tō hierō ekathezomēn didaskōn kai ouk ekratēsate me.

i18n.en: In that hour Jesus said to the crowds: "Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs, to arrest me? Day after day I sat in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me.

notes.official: *hōs epi lēstēn* 'as against a robber': *lēstēs* also means 'bandit, insurgent' (27:38, 44). *en tō hierō* 'in the temple', the precinct where teaching took place (`naos-sanctuary-hieron-temple-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: τοῦτο δὲ ὅλον γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ τῶν προφητῶν. τότε οἱ μαθηταὶ πάντες ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἔφυγον.
paragraphs.translit: touto de holon gegonen hina plērōthōsin hai graphai tōn prophētōn. tote hoi mathētai pantes aphentes auton ephygon.

i18n.en: But all this has taken place so that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled." Then all the disciples left him and fled.

paragraphs.text: Οἱ δὲ κρατήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήγαγον πρὸς Καϊάφαν τὸν ἀρχιερέα, ὅπου οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι συνήχθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de kratēsantes ton iēsoun apēgagon pros kaiaphan ton archierea, hopou hoi grammateis kai hoi presbyteroi synēchthēsan.

i18n.en: And those who had seized Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered together.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἕως τῆς αὐλῆς τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, καὶ εἰσελθὼν ἔσω ἐκάθητο μετὰ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν ἰδεῖν τὸ τέλος.
paragraphs.translit: ho de petros ēkolouthei autō apo makrothen heōs tēs aulēs tou archiereōs, kai eiselthōn esō ekathēto meta tōn hypēretōn idein to telos.

i18n.en: But Peter was following him at a distance, as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and going inside he sat with the attendants to see the end.

paragraphs.text: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τὸ συνέδριον ὅλον ἐζήτουν ψευδομαρτυρίαν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν θανατώσωσιν,
paragraphs.translit: hoi de archiereis kai to synedrion holon ezētoun pseudomartyrian kata tou iēsou hopōs auton thanatōsōsin,

i18n.en: Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking false testimony against Jesus, so that they might put him to death,

notes.official: *to synedrion holon* 'the whole council', the Sanhedrin. The Byzantine text and the KJV add *kai hoi presbyteroi* 'and elders' (see 26:3) (`critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: καὶ οὐχ εὗρον πολλῶν προσελθόντων ψευδομαρτύρων. ὕστερον δὲ προσελθόντες δύο
paragraphs.translit: kai ouch heuron pollōn proselthontōn pseudomartyrōn. hysteron de proselthontes dyo

i18n.en: and they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. But at last two came forward

notes.official: 'two came forward': the Byzantine text and the KJV add *pseudomartyres* 'two false witnesses'; the critical text leaves them unqualified, and two witnesses meet the legal requirement of Deut 19:15 (`critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: εἶπαν· Οὗτος ἔφη· Δύναμαι καταλῦσαι τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν οἰκοδομῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: eipan· houtos ephē· dynamai katalysai ton naon tou theou kai dia triōn hēmerōn oikodomēsai.

i18n.en: and said: "This man said: 'I am able to destroy the sanctuary of God and to build it in three days.'"

notes.official: *katalysai ton naon tou theou* 'to destroy the sanctuary of God': *naos*, the sanctuary building, as at 27:40 and 27:51 (`naos-sanctuary-hieron-temple-matthew`). Matthew's 'I am able to destroy' is weaker than Mark 14:58 'I will destroy'. The colon follows this wave's convention (`speech-introduction-colon-convention-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνῃ; τί οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;
paragraphs.translit: kai anastas ho archiereus eipen autō· ouden apokrinē; ti houtoi sou katamartyrousin;

i18n.en: And the high priest stood up and said to him: "Do you answer nothing? What is it that these men testify against you?"

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐσιώπα. καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐξορκίζω σε κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος ἵνα ἡμῖν εἴπῃς εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de iēsous esiōpa. kai ho archiereus eipen autō· exorkizō se kata tou theou tou zōntos hina hēmin eipēs ei sy ei ho christos ho huios tou theou.

i18n.en: But Jesus kept silent. And the high priest said to him: "I adjure you by the living God that you tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God."

notes.official: *Exorkizō se kata tou theou tou zōntos* 'I adjure you by the living God': the formal oath that obliges an answer. 'the Christ, the Son of God' (`christos-māšîaḥ-anointed-one-cross-corpus-greek-hebrew-aramaic`; `huios-theou-son-of-god-rendering-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Σὺ εἶπας· πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπʼ ἄρτι ὄψεσθε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενον ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως καὶ ἐρχόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō ho iēsous· sy eipas· plēn legō hymin, apʼ arti opsesthe ton huion tou anthrōpou kathēmenon ek dexiōn tēs dynameōs kai erchomenon epi tōn nephelōn tou ouranou.

i18n.en: Jesus says to him: "You have said it. Nevertheless I say to you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven."

notes.official: *Sy eipas* 'You have said it', as at 26:25. *plēn* 'Nevertheless'. *ek dexiōn tēs dynameōs* 'at the right hand of Power': *hē dynamis* stands for God, corresponding to Hebrew *haggəḇûrâ* 'the Might', a reverential substitute attested in rabbinic usage; the capital follows the ASV and NRSV (`tes-dynameos-the-power-mt-26-64`). The saying combines Ps 110:1 ('Sit at my right hand') with Dan 7:13 ('coming with the clouds of heaven'). *erchomenon epi tōn nephelōn tou ouranou* 'coming on the clouds of heaven' is the same wording as Mt 24:30, and both are governed by the central `son-of-man-coming-in-cloud-dan-7-13-synoptic-revelation-1-7-cross-corpus`, whose scope is extended to this verse (`son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`). *ap' arti* 'from now on'.

paragraphs.text: τότε ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς διέρρηξεν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ἐβλασφήμησεν· τί ἔτι χρείαν ἔχομεν μαρτύρων; ἴδε νῦν ἠκούσατε τὴν βλασφημίαν·
paragraphs.translit: tote ho archiereus dierrēxen ta himatia autou legōn· eblasphēmēsen· ti eti chreian echomen martyrōn; ide nyn ēkousate tēn blasphēmian·

i18n.en: Then the high priest tore his garments, saying: "He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? Behold, now you have heard the blasphemy.

notes.official: *dierrēxen ta himatia autou* 'tore his garments', the prescribed response to hearing blasphemy (m. Sanh. 7:5).

paragraphs.text: τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ; οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν· Ἔνοχος θανάτου ἐστίν.
paragraphs.translit: ti hymin dokei; hoi de apokrithentes eipan· enochos thanatou estin.

i18n.en: What do you think?" And they answered and said: "He is liable to death."

paragraphs.text: τότε ἐνέπτυσαν εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκολάφισαν αὐτόν, οἱ δὲ ἐράπισαν
paragraphs.translit: tote eneptysan eis to prosōpon autou kai ekolaphisan auton, hoi de erapisan

i18n.en: Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists; and some slapped him,

paragraphs.text: λέγοντες· Προφήτευσον ἡμῖν, χριστέ, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε;
paragraphs.translit: legontes· prophēteuson hēmin, christe, tis estin ho paisas se;

i18n.en: saying: "Prophesy to us, you Christ: who is it that struck you?"

notes.official: *Prophēteuson hēmin, christe* 'Prophesy to us, you Christ': the mockery takes up the title of 26:63 (`christos-māšîaḥ-anointed-one-cross-corpus-greek-hebrew-aramaic`).

paragraphs.text: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἐκάθητο ἔξω ἐν τῇ αὐλῇ· καὶ προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ μία παιδίσκη λέγουσα· Καὶ σὺ ἦσθα μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Γαλιλαίου·
paragraphs.translit: ho de petros ekathēto exō en tē aulē· kai prosēlthen autō mia paidiskē legousa· kai sy ēstha meta iēsou tou galilaiou·

i18n.en: Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard; and a servant girl came to him, saying: "You also were with Jesus the Galilean."

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο ἔμπροσθεν πάντων λέγων· Οὐκ οἶδα τί λέγεις.
paragraphs.translit: ho de ērnēsato emprosthen pantōn legōn· ouk oida ti legeis.

i18n.en: But he denied it before them all, saying: "I do not know what you are saying."

paragraphs.text: ἐξελθόντα δὲ εἰς τὸν πυλῶνα εἶδεν αὐτὸν ἄλλη καὶ λέγει τοῖς ἐκεῖ· Οὗτος ἦν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου·
paragraphs.translit: exelthonta de eis ton pylōna eiden auton allē kai legei tois ekei· houtos ēn meta iēsou tou nazōraiou·

i18n.en: And when he had gone out into the gateway, another servant girl saw him and says to those who were there: "This man was with Jesus the Nazarene."

notes.official: *Iēsou tou Nazōraiou* 'Jesus the Nazarene' (`proper-names-and-realia-forms-matthew`; see 2:23).

paragraphs.text: καὶ πάλιν ἠρνήσατο μετὰ ὅρκου ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
paragraphs.translit: kai palin ērnēsato meta horkou hoti ouk oida ton anthrōpon.

i18n.en: And again he denied it with an oath: "I do not know the man."

paragraphs.text: μετὰ μικρὸν δὲ προσελθόντες οἱ ἑστῶτες εἶπον τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ἀληθῶς καὶ σὺ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ, καὶ γὰρ ἡ λαλιά σου δῆλόν σε ποιεῖ·
paragraphs.translit: meta mikron de proselthontes hoi hestōtes eipon tō petrō· alēthōs kai sy ex autōn ei, kai gar hē lalia sou dēlon se poiei·

i18n.en: And after a little while those who stood by came up and said to Peter: "Truly you also are one of them, for even your speech gives you away."

notes.official: *hē lalia sou* 'your speech': Peter's Galilean accent.

paragraphs.text: τότε ἤρξατο καταθεματίζειν καὶ ὀμνύειν ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον. καὶ εὐθέως ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν·
paragraphs.translit: tote ērxato katathematizein kai omnyein hoti ouk oida ton anthrōpon. kai eutheōs alektōr ephōnēsen·

i18n.en: Then he began to call down curses and to swear: "I do not know the man." And immediately a rooster crowed.

notes.official: *katathematizein kai omnyein* 'to call down curses and to swear': the object of the curse is not stated; it may be Peter himself (if he lies) or Jesus.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τοῦ ῥήματος Ἰησοῦ εἰρηκότος ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρὶς ἀπαρνήσῃ με, καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἔξω ἔκλαυσεν πικρῶς.
paragraphs.translit: kai emnēsthē ho petros tou rhēmatos iēsou eirēkotos hoti prin alektora phōnēsai tris aparnēsē me, kai exelthōn exō eklausen pikrōs.

i18n.en: And Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken: "Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times." And he went outside and wept bitterly.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual variants: the Byzantine/TR text (KJV 'the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders') adds καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς at 26:3; similar Byzantine expansions add καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι at 26:59 ('the chief priests, and elders, and all the council') and ψευδομάρτυρες at 26:60 ('two false witnesses'). All absent from SBLGNT.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: Critical text followed at 26:3, 59, 60; Byzantine additions recorded.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual variant: the critical text reads τὸ αἷμά μου τῆς διαθήκης ('my blood of the covenant'); the Byzantine/TR text (KJV 'my blood of the new testament') reads τῆς καινῆς διαθήκης, assimilating to Lk 22:20 / 1 Cor 11:25. Also unglossed: διαθήκη 'covenant' (ASV) vs. 'testament' (KJV).
editorial_questions_resolved.default_taken: my blood of the covenant (critical text)
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'my blood of the covenant' (critical text); 'new' and KJV 'testament' recorded.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: σκανδαλίζομαι ἐν ἐμοί (also 26:33; precedent 13:21 'falls away', 13:57 'took offense'): 'fall away because of me' vs. 'be offended in me' (ASV/KJV) vs. 'stumble because of me'.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'fall away' kept at 26:31, 33 (consistent with published 13:21); 'were offended' at 15:12 (cf. published 13:57).

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual variant: the Byzantine/TR text (KJV 'if this cup may not pass away from me') adds τὸ ποτήριον and ἀπ᾽ ἐμοῦ; the critical text reads only εἰ οὐ δύναται τοῦτο παρελθεῖν ('if this cannot pass').
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: Critical text followed; Byzantine 'this cup ... from me' recorded.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Ἑταῖρε, ἐφʼ ὃ πάρει (Hetaire, eph' ho parei): an elliptical crux. Command 'Friend, do that for which you have come' (ASV) vs. question 'Friend, why are you here?' (KJV 'wherefore art thou come?') vs. exclamation 'Friend, so this is what you are here for!'
editorial_questions_resolved.default_taken: Friend, do that for which you have come
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: Imperative 'Friend, do that for which you have come' kept (ASV, NRSV); question and exclamation readings in commentary.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Canon-wording difference and lexical choice: TBWTT ch. 4 quotes 26:52-53 as « Remets ton sabre en place (…). Crois-tu que je ne pourrais pas faire appel à mon père, qui mettrait à l'instant à ma disposition plus de douze légions d'anges ? ». παραστήσει μοι literally 'will place beside me / put at my disposal'; ASV 'send me'. παρακαλέσαι 'appeal to' (canon « faire appel ») vs. ASV 'beseech'.
